accessibility: The dialog has a title and a description, a visible close control, and keeps a visible 2px primary focus outline on every control.
Discard and leave is the destructive choice and is told apart by its label and its red look, not by color alone.
constraints: Built only from Adapter Widgets (Panel dialog, Stack, Button); no Widget outside the Adapter catalog.
Every visible string is bound with $i18n; en-US and zh-TW keep identical key sets.
Visual language follows the Quiet Canvas design system in DESIGN.md.
entryConditions: A person with unsaved edits in the Flow editor (the toolbar shows Unsaved changes) followed a link to another page or to another Flow; the navigation waits for this answer. Closing the tab asks the browser's own question instead.
The dialog has one state; leaving with nothing unsaved raises no prompt, and neither does moving within the same Flow.
The render context selects one Workspace viewport preset, one Locale and one theme; the dialog is centered over a dimmed ground.
spec.intent: Show the prompt that the UX Flow editor raises when a person leaves a Flow that has unsaved edits, as built from Adapter Widgets only: stay and keep editing, or discard the edits and go.
interactionRules: Keep editing closes the dialog and the person stays on the Flow with the edits intact; Escape and the close control do the same.
Discard and leave drops the draft and completes the navigation that was waiting.
